I found the quoted words on the page exactly as reported. The candidate fails part 3: "the coming weeks" doesn't give a length of time.

**The page.** The link opened. It's singjupost.com's full transcript of the Google I/O 2018 keynote, which the page dates Tuesday, 8 May 2018. The sentence is in Pichai's part of the Google Duplex demo, right after he describes Google calling businesses to update their opening hours over holidays: "This is going to be rolling out as an experiment in the coming weeks, and so stay tuned." The page is a transcript, not a news report, so it counts as a primary source.

**The four parts of the rule:**
1. **Role: passes.** Pichai had been chief executive of Google since 2 October 2015, and Google builds frontier models.
2. **Forward-looking and about AI: passes.** Duplex is an AI system, and the words say it will be used for real, as a trial calling businesses.
3. **Date or length of time: fails.** "The coming weeks" doesn't say how many weeks. The ledger already treats "the next few months" and "the coming months" as undated because they name no length, and "the coming weeks" works the same way. That "coming months" reading was the agent's own application and is flagged for the method owner, not ruled by them, and it doesn't mention weeks. So check that this extension is acceptable. If it isn't, the candidate becomes borderline, not admitted.
4. **Primary source: passes.** It's a transcript.

**Already recorded?** No. The only recorded file from the same day is about the John Legend voice "later this year", which is a different claim.
